instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Synthetic materials are a group of materials which do not occur naturally. They were invented by people and are made artificially, from chemicals. They are often referred to as plastics.
Most plastics are made using crude oil. Earth only has a limited supply of crude oil. Therefore, new processes are being developed to make plastics from other raw materials such as plant matter.
There are many methods of making plastics, each giving the finished material different properties. For example, plastics can be hard or soft, transparent or opaque, plain or colourful.
Some plastics can be moulded using heat after they have set. Other plastics can only be shaped once.

atoms.a: What are synthetic materials made from?
Which oil is usually used to make plastics?
Which properties are typical of plastics?

instruction.text: Plastics often have long, complicated names. Therefore, we sometimes use abbreviations to label them. Which abbreviation could match which plastic?

atoms.a: Which raw material are people trying to make plastic out of?
What can be made out of plastic?

hint.text: There may be more than one right answer.

instruction.text: Roughly how long would it take for this object to break down in the natural environment?
